**Written Statement**
**Regarding: Afternoon Route 9, Bus 41 — October 27**
**Student: Amara Okafor, Kindergarten, Fairmont Elementary**
**From: [Driver Name], School Bus Driver**
**To: Mrs. Okafor**
**Date submitted: November 13**

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

My name is [Driver Name]. I am the school bus driver on Bus 41, Route 9 elementary. My supervisor, Darlene, asked me to write a formal statement about the complaint dated October 29, which I received on November 3. I understand a copy of this statement will go to you, and I am submitting it by the November 13 deadline. I want to explain what happened from my side, why I did what I did, and ask that the bus camera footage be pulled.

On Tuesday, October 27, on the afternoon run, I was driving Bus 41 on Route 9 elementary. Amara Okafor was one of the students on my bus. She is in kindergarten at Fairmont Elementary, and she had the green tag on her bag. The green tag means an adult has to be at the stop for her to get off. That is the district rule for kindergarten riders, and I follow it.

The stop is Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street. My schedule says 3:50. I arrived at 3:52. I waited until about 3:55. I looked at the corner and did not see an adult there. I understand from the complaint that you were parked across Brandt by the laundromat and that you waved. I did not see you. I am not saying you were not there or that you did not wave. I am saying that from my seat on the bus, I did not see you, and there was a box truck parked on that side of the street. I was not ignoring you. I cannot leave the bus with students aboard to walk across the road and look around. That would not be safe.

Because I did not see an adult at the stop, I kept Amara on the bus, per the district rule. I radioed dispatch at 3:56. Gloria at dispatch called the school. I still had three more stops and 14 students still on the bus. I finished the route and brought Amara back to Fairmont Elementary at 4:31. I walked her into the office myself and left her with Mrs. Petrakis.

Amara was fine. She was coloring on her folder. She asked me if she could ride more, and I told her we were going on a little extra trip. I did not take her anywhere except back to school. I understand the complaint says I “took” her. I want to be clear that I kept her on the bus because she is a kindergartner and no adult was at the stop, and I returned her to school as the rule requires.

I also understand the complaint says I drove off laughing. I was not laughing. As we pulled out, I was telling the fourth grader in seat 2 to sit back down. That is what I was doing. I did not drive off laughing at your daughter.

I understand you were scared. I have grandkids, and if one of them was kept on a bus, I would be worried too until I knew what was happening. I am sorry you and Amara had a bad afternoon. I am not going to apologize for following the rule, because I believe keeping a kindergartner on the bus when no adult is at the stop is the right and safe thing to do. But I am sorry that it was upsetting for your family.

Years ago, I had a similar situation on my route with a different family. I kept the child on the bus and brought them back to school, and the family thanked me afterward once they understood the rule. I am not bringing that up to argue. I am bringing it up because this is not something I did to be difficult. It is how I have been trained to keep the children safe.

I am asking the Transportation Office to pull the bus camera footage from Bus 41 for the afternoon of October 27, from about 3:50 to 3:56, and to keep it with this complaint. The footage should show the stop, how long I waited, and what was visible from the bus. I want the record to be complete.

I am also asking, respectfully, if you can wait on the bus side of Brandt Street or step out of your car where I can see you. I will watch for you. I am not saying this to blame you. I am saying it because I want to see you and let Amara off with you. If there is a truck parked there again, it may block my view, and I do not want either of us to go through this again.

I am glad to keep driving Amara. I want this fixed. I have driven for 28 years and have not had a write-up. I take my job seriously, and I take the safety of every child on my bus seriously. I am willing to talk with you or with the Transportation Office about how to make the stop work better.

Respectfully,
[Driver Name]
School Bus Driver, Bus 41
Route 9 Elementary
